S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S056.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
S056.description: Excessive anxiety and worry (expectant apprehension) occurring persistently about a number of events or activities.

subtypes.Chronic Worry: Worry occurs more days than not for at least 6 months.
subtypes.Generalized Worry: Worry is not confined to specific topics but spreads to various domains like work, school, family, and finances.
subtypes.Catastrophizing: Jumping to conclusions that minor mistakes or events will lead to irreversible disasters.
subtypes.Intolerance of Uncertainty: Unable to tolerate future uncertainty, trapped in 'what if' questions.

S057.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
S057.description: The subjective experience of finding it difficult to stop or control the worry.

subtypes.Failure to Control: Unable to regulate worry despite efforts to stop or distract oneself.
subtypes.Intrusive Worry: Worries suddenly intrude into the mind and interfere with focus while doing other tasks.
subtypes.Chaining of Worry: One worry triggers another in a chain reaction, escalating to catastrophic thoughts.

S058.name: Restlessness_Tension
S058.description: Restlessness, or feeling keyed up or on edge.

subtypes.Feeling Keyed Up: Feeling anxious and wound up like a spring, unable to stay still.
subtypes.Physical Tension: The entire body feels stiff and tense, unable to relax.
subtypes.Nervousness: Nerves are on edge, being startled easily by minor sounds or stimuli.

S061.name: Muscle_Tension
S061.description: A state where muscles are continuously tense, stiff, and accompanied by discomfort.

subtypes.Neck and Shoulder Tension: Muscles in the shoulders and back of the neck are knotted and stiff, causing pain or headaches.
subtypes.Jaw Tension: Clenching teeth or tension in the jaw causing jaw pain or headaches.
subtypes.Generalized Muscle Aches: Muscles all over the body, including back, arms, and legs, are stiff, painful, and easily fatigued.
subtypes.Chronic Stiffness: Muscles remain in a constant state of tension and do not relax.

symptom.disease_info: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is characterized by persistent, excessive worry and apprehensive expectation about multiple life domains (such as work, health, finances, or family) occurring more days than not for at least several months. The worry is typically experienced as difficult to control and is accompanied by physical and cognitive manifestations like fatigue, muscle tension, restlessness, difficulty concentrating, and sleep disturbance. It often has a chronic, fluctuating course, with periods of exacerbation in response to stressors but without being limited to discrete panic attacks or specific feared situations. Clinically, GAD is distinguished from normal worry by its pervasiveness, duration, and degree of impairment, and from other anxiety disorders by the broad range of concerns rather than a focus on particular phobic objects, panic episodes, or traumatic triggers.

patient.stressor: Roughly nine months ago, Sonia’s husband was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes and mild congestive heart failure, and she took on the role of coordinating his medications, dietary changes, and frequent medical appointments. At the same time, she was heavily involved in planning the new multicultural senior art center, running her book club, and helping with community garden responsibilities, leaving her feeling increasingly stretched between caregiving duties and longstanding community commitments. Over the next seven months, she found herself double- and triple-checking pill organizers, second-guessing every meal she cooked for her husband, and rearranging museum tours and garden work when appointments shifted, which gradually eroded the sense of enjoyment she usually derived from her cultural activities. She ultimately sought psychiatric care after her primary care physician noticed how tense and keyed up she appeared during a routine visit, and she admitted that the strain of managing her husband’s health and her many roles had become overwhelming and was starting to sap the pleasure from her retirement.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel like I’m constantly bracing myself—my whole body stays tight all day from worrying about my husband and everything I’m juggling.”
